heroHeadline: JNIM Siege of Bamako Enters Day 6 — Russia Refuses to Withdraw as France Evacuates Nationals
heroSubtitle: Russia formally rejected JNIM's demand for Africa Corps withdrawal on April 30, framing the catastrophic April 25–30 offensive — which killed Defence Minister Camara, lost Kidal, Tessit, Labbezanga, and Ménaka's urban core — as a 'foiled coup.' Bamako's nightly curfew entered its fifth night as French nationals boarded last commercial flights under an evacuation advisory. At least 13,000 Malians have fled to neighboring countries. The Long War Journal characterized the April 25–30 JNIM-FLA offensive as the largest AQ-affiliated operation in years. Burkina Faso adopted a draft law to create a 100,000-strong military reserve by end of 2026. The AES Unified Force pledged joint operations while JNIM holds Tessit, FLA holds Kidal, and ISGS besieges FAMa in Ménaka's former UN camp.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, RFI, Le Monde, Crisis Group, UN OHCHR, HRW, SIPRI, AFP, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Long War Journal, Africa Center for Strategic Studies, and Institute for Economics & Peace. All figures approximate unless stated.
